summary: The document provides a high-level functional overview of a Hospital Management System (HMS), listing core modules (EMR, Billing, Pharmacy, etc.) and a generic tech stack (React, FastAPI, PostgreSQL). However, it lacks specific technical specifications, data models, API contracts, and critical healthcare compliance details (HIPAA/GDPR), making it insufficient for immediate engineering implementation.

risk_factors.title: Lack of Specific PHI Encryption Standards
risk_factors.description: The document mentions 'password encryption' and 'privacy of medical information' but does not specify AES-256 for PHI at rest or TLS 1.2+ for data in transit, which are mandatory for HIPAA compliance.
risk_factors.mitigation: Explicitly mandate AES-256-GCM for all PHI fields at rest and enforce TLS 1.2/1.3 for all API communications. Define key management strategies (e.g., KMS).

verification.claim: Risk: Lack of Specific PHI Encryption Standards — The document mentions 'password encryption' and 'privacy of medical information' but does not specify AES-256 for PHI at rest or TLS 1.2+ for data in transit, which are mandatory for HIPAA compliance.

risk_factors.title: Ambiguous Audit Trail Requirements
risk_factors.description: The document lists 'audit logs' as a feature but does not specify immutability, retention periods, or specific events to be logged (e.g., who accessed which patient record and when).
risk_factors.mitigation: Define an immutable audit log schema (append-only database or WORM storage) capturing user ID, action, timestamp, IP, and resource ID for all PHI access. Set retention to 6+ years per HIPAA.

verification.claim: Risk: Ambiguous Audit Trail Requirements — The document lists 'audit logs' as a feature but does not specify immutability, retention periods, or specific events to be logged (e.g., who accessed which patient record and when).

risk_factors.title: Missing Interoperability Standards
risk_factors.description: No mention of HL7 FHIR or DICOM standards, which are critical for exchanging medical records and imaging data with other healthcare providers and devices.
risk_factors.mitigation: Integrate HL7 FHIR R4 API endpoints for patient demographics and clinical data. Support DICOM for imaging storage and retrieval if radiology is included.

risk_factors.title: Undefined Disaster Recovery Metrics
risk_factors.description: The document mentions 'backup/recovery' and 'high availability' but lacks specific RTO (Recovery Time Objective) and RPO (Recovery Point Objective) benchmarks.
risk_factors.mitigation: Define RTO < 1 hour and RPO < 5 minutes for critical patient data. Specify automated failover mechanisms and backup frequency (e.g., continuous replication).

risk_factors.title: Generic Authentication Without MFA
risk_factors.description: The document suggests 'JWT/OAuth-based authentication' but does not mandate Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) for privileged roles (Admin, Doctor), which is a best practice for healthcare systems.
risk_factors.mitigation: Enforce MFA for all staff roles. Implement step-up authentication for sensitive actions like exporting patient data or modifying billing.

ai_recommendations: Expand the document to include a detailed Data Flow Diagram (DFD) showing how PHI moves between modules, highlighting encryption points and access controls.
Add a specific section on 'Security Architecture' detailing network segmentation, firewall rules, and intrusion detection systems (IDS) suitable for a healthcare environment.
Define the 'Non-Functional Requirements' with quantifiable metrics: e.g., 'API response time < 200ms at p95', 'System uptime 99.95%', 'RTO < 1 hour', 'RPO < 5 minutes'.
Include a 'Compliance Checklist' mapping each functional requirement to specific HIPAA Security Rule standards (e.g., 45 CFR 164.312) and GDPR articles.
Specify the technology stack versions and containerization strategy (e.g., Docker/Kubernetes) to ensure reproducibility and security patching.
